'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Order of battle for the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
****[[Chief of the General Staff (Russia)|Chief of the General Staff]] of the [[Russian Armed Forces]] [[Valery Gerasimov]] is appointed commander of the Joint Group of Forces participating in the war with [[Ukraine]]. Generals [[Oleg Salyukov]], {{ill|Alexei Kim|ru|Ким, Алексей Ростиславович}}, and [[Sergei Surovikin]], who previously held this position, become his deputies. *[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[Islamic State–Taliban conflict]]
***[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Afghanistan bombing]]
****An [[Islamic State – Khorasan Province|Islamic State]] [[Suicide attack|suicide bomber]] blows himself up at the entrance of the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Afghanistan)|foreign ministry]] offices in [[Kabul]], [[Afghanistan]], killing at least 20 people and many others injured. '''Health and environment'''
*[[2022 Uganda Ebola outbreak]]
**[[Uganda]]n [[Ministry of Health (Uganda)|Health Minister]] [[Jane Aceng]] declares an end to the outbreak of [[Sudan ebolavirus|Sudan ''ebolavirus'']] in the country that has killed 77 people since September. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/uganda-declares-end-ebola-outbreak-2023-01-11/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Japan–United States relations]]
**[[United States Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] announces that [[Japan]] and the [[United States]] will include [[space warfare]] as a trigger for the [[Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security between the United States and Japan|Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security]]. [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/world/857126/us-japan-agree-space-attacks-covered-by-joint-defense-treaty/story/ (AFP via GMA News Online)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Five people are killed and 13 others injured when a man [[vehicle-ramming attack|rams his vehicle]] into a crowd in [[Guangzhou]], [[China]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-64245246 (BBC News)]
*Six people are injured in a [[mass stabbing]] at the [[Gare du Nord]] train station in [[Paris]], [[France]]. The attacker is shot by police, arrested, and hospitalized. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-64234281 (BBC News)]
*[[Joe Biden classified documents incident]]
**Aides to the [[President of the United States]] [[Joe Biden]] discover a second set of classified documents besides those found on Monday in a [[Washington, D.C.]] office. The [[White House]] acknowledges the discovery. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/white-house/biden-aides-find-second-batch-classified-documents-new-location-rcna65371 (NBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[2023 FAA system outage]]
**For the first time since [[September 11, 2001|9/11]], the [[Federal Aviation Administration|FAA]] issues a nationwide [[ground stop]] in the [[United States]] following the failure of the FAA's [[NOTAM]] system. [https://www.cnbc.com/2023/01/11/us-faa-says-flight-personnel-alert-system-not-processing-updates-after-outage.html (CNBC)]
*The launch of an unmanned [[ABL Space Systems]] RS1 rocket fails at the [[Pacific Spaceport Complex – Alaska]] in [[Kodiak, Alaska|Kodiak]], [[Alaska]], [[United States]]. The rocket crashes during the launch, damaging the launch platform and destroying the rocket and its cargo. [https://www.adn.com/business-economy/2023/01/11/abl-rocket-crashes-after-liftoff-from-kodiak-spaceport-damages-launch-pad/ (''Anchorage Daily News'')]
*The [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Postal services in the United Kingdom|postal service]] [[Royal Mail]] tells people to stop sending mail abroad due to a "cyber incident" that is causing severe disruption to mail delivery, with "minor delays" to mail coming into the UK also being reported. It is later confirmed to be a [[ransomware]] attack from a [[Russia]]-linked [[hacker group]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-64231473 (BBC News)]
